input.quote: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
input.rationale: The IP package meets the preferred position in full, so no redline is warranted. § 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for Customer in Customer on creation and contains an express present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest (plus personnel assignments and further-assurance). § 14.3, read with the § 1.8 definition, confirms Vendor retains only its pre-existing Vendor Technology, and § 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works from Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and that Vendor receives only a limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer — service delivery, not independent exploitation — reinforced by § 15.1's bar on sale, advertising, cross-customer combination and model training. § 14.4 negates joint ownership absent a separately signed instrument, and limits feedback use to generalized suggestions while Customer retains unrestricted rights in its own feedback. Two points are noted only for the record and are not deviations: Deliverable ownership is "subject to payment of the applicable Fees" (customary), and the § 1.3 carve-out of anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User or an individual is an acceptable de-identified-telemetry exclusion.
